roots.note: separate operator-source grammar parsed before ordinary source; deliberately not reachable from compilation-unit

notes: Appendix C is normative and governs where an older example elsewhere in language-ref.md conflicts.

All 49 productions unreachable from compilation-unit are classified. None is accidental: 18 are scanner rules, 8 are filename-classification rules used by the compiler before parsing, 14 belong to the operator-source grammar rooted at operator-source-file, 8 are the non-normative informative-* control-flow shapes, and 1 is the builtin-collection-type-name registry consulted by typed-collection-literal-guard.
The C.5 match production retains zero-or-more .case arms because Appendix C specifies that parser shape.
Context-sensitive restrictions are represented by zero-width guards rather than encoded as misleading context-free productions.

RESOLVED: the body section on pre-declared operator glyphs previously stated they were available for overload and showed an example. It now states the C.10 alpha rule: the lexer recognizes the glyph, the parser rejects its use as an expression operator, and no project may supply an overload. No code example overloads a glyph.

RESOLVED: parenthesized-type-list previously admitted only unnamed type-list items, which could not spell the named generic arguments the reference writes as `co.core.Map->(key co.lang.string, val co.lang.int)` and `LinkedList->(T co.lang.int)`. It now shares return-item-list's optionally-named shape, which is what the parser's arrow tail already accepts. C.11 records the three readings of a type's arrow tail.

RESOLVED: the Disclaimer now exempts @co.* directives, annotations, pragmas and decorators from the table-listed-without-an-example rejection rule, which conflicted with C.7's unsupported-feature parse error. C.7.1 records the split: an @co.* metadata form is parsed through the single annotation production, collected, and silently ignored when unimplemented, while a reserved co.* name in declaration-kind, type, callable or operator position is still rejected.

RESOLVED: the Disclaimer's operator rule — a pre-defined operator the language has not registered raises an unsupported-feature error on USE — now holds in every position. predeclared-operator-glyph was already refused in both operand and infix position; reserved-operator was refused only in operand position, so `a ->> b` reported a missing ";" and named the terminator instead of the reserved operator. The Pratt infix loop now refuses it as well, and TestPredefinedUnregisteredOperatorIsUnsupportedInEveryPosition covers operand, infix and postfix position for all six reserved spellings and for the glyphs.

RESOLVED: the reference now carries a Builtin Collections registry and spells every built-in collection with an initial capital (co.core.List, co.core.Set, co.core.Map, co.core.Tree, co.core.Trie, co.core.Array, co.core.Tuple), replacing the earlier lowercase co.core.list/map/array spellings. builtin-collection-type-name records that closed set, and typed-collection-literal-guard now tests the prefix against it, against an alias-directive binding to one of those names, or against a user-declared collection type, rather than against an unbounded notion of a collection type.

The grammar keeps C.4.1's typed-collection-literal verbatim, so its first alternative still spells only the array and map bodies. The no-arrow-tail Type( ... ) collection value that C.4.1 exemplifies as co.core.Set(1,2,3) and C.4.2 lists as a contextual reading is carried by postfix-expression's call-suffix over the identical source span under the same guard, so nothing is unparseable; the grammar records this in the comment above the production rather than by diverging from Appendix C.

OPEN: typed-collection-literal and typed-collection-literal-guard are specified by C.4.1/C.4.2 and reachable from compilation-unit, but the alpha parser does not implement them. TestGrammarProductionsHaveImplementationTrace reports both as untraced. The grammar is normative, so this is a parser gap rather than a grammar defect. `go run ./cmd/refblocks` confirms it from the corpora side: the Collections section block (language-ref.md line 8684) and the three C.4.1 blocks (lines 10009, 10017, 10025) do not parse and are awaiting classification.
